title: Relapse Risk Assessment Scale
short: A self-assessment of early relapse warning signs for people in recovery from substance use, to help in early identification and prompt intervention.

intro.measures: Assessing the risk of relapse in individuals with Substance Use Disorder (SUD) can help in early identification and prompt intervention. This tool can be used by individuals in recovery or by clinicians as part of a therapeutic process.
intro.instructions: Please read each statement below and rate how much it has applied to you in the past week on a scale from 0 to 4.

questions.text: I have felt overwhelmed by my emotions (e.g., anxiety, sadness).
I find myself denying or minimizing problems that are clearly important.
I have noticed an increase in negative thoughts about myself or my recovery.
I feel complacent about my recovery process.
I have been romanticizing my past substance use.
I have skipped meetings or therapy sessions that are part of my recovery plan.
I have engaged in behaviors that I previously associated with substance use.
I have spent time with people who use substances or encourage my use.
I have found myself lying or being secretive about my activities or feelings.
I have neglected important responsibilities at work, home, or school.
I have experienced physical cravings for substances.
I have put myself in situations where substances are available, thinking I can resist.
I am facing new or worsening financial or legal problems that stress me.
I have been using healthy coping strategies less frequently than before.
I feel less connected to or supported by my sober network or support groups.
I have had thoughts about using substances as a way to cope with my current situation.

bands.label: Low apparent risk of relapse
bands.text: Continue practicing coping strategies and maintaining support networks.

bands.label: Moderate risk of relapse
bands.text: It may be beneficial to increase support, whether through more frequent therapy sessions, support group meetings, or by enhancing your relapse prevention strategies.

bands.label: High risk of relapse
bands.text: Strongly consider reaching out for additional support from a therapist, counselor, or support group. It may be necessary to revisit and strengthen your relapse prevention plan.

note: Remember, this tool is for self-assessment purposes and is not a substitute for professional advice.
next_steps: Regardless of your score, it's important to discuss your results with a healthcare professional, counselor, or support group who can provide personalized feedback and guidance.
